text:
sasha: quick follow-up from the CP separation RFC — proposing a small new pattern: a lightweight per-tenant "connector adapter" that only handles ephemeral TLS/session relay + auth token translation. keeps full control plane isolated. thoughts?

ana: curious — how is this different than the existing relay? sounds like sidecarless vs sidecar debate all over again :thinking_face:

mike: short answer: adapter is strictly ephemeral, no long-lived peering, no ENI. it terminates inbound TLS from customer VPC, mints short-lived session creds, then forwards to regional relay pool. cheaper egress, less route churn.

jeff: that reduces our per-tenant public IP usage, right? how do we guarantee ip-preservation if customers expect source address?

sasha: good point. not preserving source IP by default. we can offer opt-in NAT-preservation mode that pins a small elastic pool per-customer but only for customers who pay commit. default is SNAT -> regional pool.

priya: what about certs? connectors will need to present tenant certs for mutual TLS to CP. do we push certs into customer VPC or use SNI passthrough?

mike: I sketched two flows:

- flow A: connector terminates mTLS using tenant certs stored in our KMS but provisioned via control-plane API. connector rotates every 12h.
- flow B: passthrough to tenant-provided backend (requires private endpoint + route) — more ops for customer.

sasha: Flow A wins for onboarding speed. Flow B for highly reg customers.

ana: ops-mode question: how do we do health/fallover? connectors are ephemeral — if adapter dies mid-session, do we reconnect to a different connector? any session affinity required?

jeff: we should keep session metadata in an external cheap store (Dynamo/cached controlplane) and reconnect clients to new connector with session cookie. session resume within 5s window.

mike: batching idea: connectors can do prefix-KV caching for LLM contexts to reduce tokens upstream. but any caching at adapter increases surface area for correctness/regression. need TTL and invalidation.

priya: security: connectors talk to CP over private peering. what about egress isolation if CP is multi-tenant? should use dedicated VPC peering per region and per tier, with routing policies.

sasha: agreed. design would be: connectors in customer VPCs (or ephemeral hosted relay in tenant subnet) -> private peering to regional CP ingress -> regional relay pool -> model serving. connectors only accept inbound, no direct model calls.

mike: config sketch (very rough):
```
connector:
  mode: ephemeral
  cert_source: controlplane-kms
  session_ttl: 300
  nat_mode: snat | preserve
  cache_ttl_ms: 100
```

ana: TL;DR? I want bullet tradeoffs:
- Pros: faster onboarding, lower long-lived IP footprint, easier cert rotation, cheaper for small tenants.
- Cons: harder source-IP preservation, more session resume complexity, cache correctness risk, more moving pieces for compliance.

jeff: Ops checklist if we pilot:
- rollout to 10 alpha customers behind feature flag
- telemetry: per-connector token/time-to-first-byte, session-resume-rate, cache-hit-rate
- rollback: instant disable adapter via CP policy and fallback to private endpoint peering

priya: + add DDoS/abuse throttles on connector layer and per-tenant circuit breakers.

deploy-bot: deployment started for connector-prototype -> canary region: us-west-2 at 3349876600 :rocket:

mike: will write a short spike doc with sequence diagrams and health/failover story. assigning to me + priya.

sasha: thanks all — can we sync tomorrow 10am to pick alpha candidates? :calendar:
